verdict.headline: Retail sales' sharpest drop in a year rattles stocks but weekly gains hold
verdict.label: HOLD — 2 of 3 regime triggers breached: WTI $82.40 and Brent $88.52 above oil thresholds; 30Y at 5.24%, 4bps below 5.28% gate; BTC $63,074 tonight holds $62K floor with $1,074 buffer; RDDT inclusion Monday, FOMC Minutes Wednesday, PMI Flash Friday
verdict.rationale_short: Saturday: no equity session. Carrying forward Friday's close — S&P 500 7,785.76 (-0.17%), Nasdaq 26,776 (-0.10%) — which completed the third consecutive weekly gain despite the session's sharp headwind: July retail sales at -0.6% MoM (largest monthly drop in >1 year) and UMich preliminary sentiment collapsing to 51.0 from 55.2 vs 54.5 expected. The critical read: the 30Y fully reversed its pre-market compression to 5.19%, closing at 5.24% — the bond market signaling soft consumer data alone is insufficient to move the long end. Both oil benchmarks remain above regime thresholds (WTI $82.40, Brent $88.52) on Bessent's Iran 'economic isolation' threat. BTC firms to $63,074 overnight (Crypto.com) from Friday's $62,945, buffering the $62K gate by $1,074. The week ahead is a four-event sequence: RDDT mechanical inclusion auction Monday Aug 18 close; FOMC Minutes Wednesday Aug 19; PMI Flash Friday Aug 21; then NVDA Aug 26 and Warsh at Jackson Hole Aug 28. The binary: do the Minutes flag dovish intent consistent with the soft consumer data, or does PMI flash services show reacceleration that pushes September hike odds above 40% before Warsh speaks?

bear_case: The bond market delivered the week's clearest signal: the 30Y refused to hold 5.19% compression even on the softest consumer print in >1 year (-0.6% retail, UMich 51.0), closing back at 5.24%. If the long end won't move on that data, the bar for dovish movement before Jackson Hole is structurally higher than current equity valuations imply. The 5.24% close sits 24bps above the level that would meaningfully relieve growth-multiple pressure on the S&P 500, and the only credible path there before September 15 runs through Warsh's Aug 28 keynote — itself dependent on PMI flash services not reaccelerating before he speaks. Oil is a structurally embedded inflation input that Bessent's Iran threat has now amplified: WTI $82.40 and Brent $88.52 are both above regime thresholds with the SPR at 40-year lows. The altitude ceiling now has four sector confirmations — CSCO, AMAT, AVGO, and AMAT's AH reset — entering NVDA's Aug 26 print. A consumer sector printing -0.6% MoM retail growth while sentiment erodes to 51.0 does not easily reverse in the two weeks between now and Jackson Hole. The constructive case requires three sequential outcomes in sequence over 12 days: FOMC Minutes dovish, PMI flat-to-soft, and NVDA beats cleanly. All three must land; any one failure cascades.
